q.t: How many end points does a line segment have?
q.e: A segment is a piece of a line with a definite start and finish.

q.t: How many end points does a ray have?
q.e: A ray starts at one point and goes on for ever in one direction, like a torch beam.

q.t: How many end points does a line have?
q.e: A line goes on for ever in both directions.

q.t: A point has:
q.e: A point only marks a place; the dot we draw is just a picture of it.

q.t: How many lines can be drawn through two given points?
q.e: Two points fix the direction completely, so there is exactly one straight line through them.

q.t: Which of these has a length that can be measured?
q.e: Only a segment ends at both sides; lines and rays go on for ever.

q.t: A ray extends endlessly in:
q.e: It is fixed at its starting point and goes on the other way only.

q.t: A flat surface that extends endlessly in all directions is called a:
q.e: A table top or a wall is a small part of a plane.

q.t: Two lines that meet at a point are called:
q.e: Intersect means cross; the meeting place is the point of intersection.

q.t: Three or more points lying on the same line are called:
q.e: ‘Co-linear’ means sharing the same line.

q.t: How many lines can be drawn through a single point?
q.e: A line through one point can still turn to any direction, so there is no limit.

q.t: Three points are not on one line. How many line segments join them in pairs?
q.e: AB, BC and CA — the three sides of a triangle.

q.t: At how many points can two different straight lines cross at most?
q.e: If they shared two points they would be the same line.

q.t: Three or more lines passing through the same point are called:
q.e: Concurrent means ‘running together’ to one point.

q.t: B lies between A and C on a line. AB = 5 cm and BC = 3 cm. Find AC (in cm).
q.e: The two parts make up the whole: 5 + 3.

q.t: A segment is 10 cm long. How far is its midpoint from either end (in cm)?
q.e: The midpoint cuts the segment into two equal halves.

q.t: Ray AB and ray BA are different because they:
q.e: A ray is named from its starting point: AB starts at A, BA starts at B, and they go in opposite directions.

q.t: How many rays can start from one point?
q.e: One in every possible direction.

q.t: Two edges of a table meet at a corner. The corner is a model of a:
q.e: Two lines meet at a point.

q.t: Lines in the same plane that never meet are called:
q.e: They stay the same distance apart everywhere.

q.t: A, B, C and D are four points on a line. How many different line segments do they form?
q.e: AB, AC, AD, BC, BD, CD. Each pair of points gives one segment: 4 × 3 ÷ 2 = 6.

q.t: Four points are placed so that no three are on one line. How many lines pass through pairs of them?
q.e: Each pair gives a different line: 4 × 3 ÷ 2 = 6.

q.t: What is the greatest number of points at which 3 straight lines can cross each other?
q.e: Each pair of lines can cross once, and there are 3 pairs.

q.t: AC = 12 cm, B is the midpoint of AC and D is the midpoint of BC. Find AD (in cm).
q.e: AB = BC = 6. BD = 3. So AD = AB + BD = 9.

q.t: P, Q and R are on a line with Q between P and R. PQ = 7 cm and QR = 4 cm. Find PR (in cm).
q.e: PR = PQ + QR.

q.t: Five points are placed so that no three are on one line. How many lines pass through pairs of them?
q.e: Each of the 5 points pairs with 4 others, but that counts every line twice: 20 ÷ 2 = 10.

q.t: A segment 9.6 cm long is bisected. How long is each part (in cm)?
q.e: Bisect means cut into two equal parts.

q.t: X is a point on segment AB with AX = 2 × XB. If AB = 12 cm, find AX (in cm).
q.e: AB is 3 equal parts of 4 cm; AX is 2 of them.

q.t: A, B and C are on a line with B between A and C. How many rays start from B along this line?
q.e: Ray BA and ray BC — one in each direction.

q.t: The length of a line is:
q.e: A line has no end points, so it has no measurable length.

q.t: What is the greatest number of crossing points 5 straight lines can have?
q.e: Every pair of lines can cross once: 5 × 4 ÷ 2 = 10 pairs.

q.t: Six points lie on a line. How many different line segments do they form?
q.e: One segment for each pair of points: 6 × 5 ÷ 2 = 15.

q.t: A, B, C, D lie on a line in that order. AB = 3 cm, BC = 4 cm and CD = 5 cm. Find AC + BD (in cm).
q.e: AC = 7 and BD = 9. BC is counted in both.

q.t: Ten points are placed so that no three are on one line. How many lines pass through pairs of them?
AB = 20 cm. M is the midpoint of AB and N is the midpoint of AM. Find NB (in cm).
q.e: AM = 10, AN = 5. NB = AB − AN = 15.

q.t: Three points lie on a line and a fourth point is off it. How many different lines pass through at least two of these points?
q.e: The one line through the three collinear points, plus one line from the outside point to each of them: 1 + 3 = 4.

q.t: Five points are placed so that no three are on one line. How many triangles have these points as vertices?
q.e: Choose 3 of the 5 points: 5 × 4 × 3 ÷ 6 = 10.

q.t: P divides segment AB (15 cm) so that AP : PB = 2 : 3. Find AP (in cm).
q.e: 5 equal parts of 3 cm. AP is 2 parts.

q.t: AB = 7 cm, BC = 3 cm and AC = 4 cm, with all three points on one line. Which point lies between the other two?
q.e: The two shorter lengths add to the longest: AC + CB = 4 + 3 = 7 = AB. So C is between A and B.

q.t: Into how many regions do 4 straight lines divide a plane at most?
q.e: Start with 1 region. The 1st line adds 1, the 2nd adds 2, the 3rd adds 3, the 4th adds 4: 1 + 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 11.
